newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils expected quiet despite lower palm oi.
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils expected quiet despite lower palm oi.

text.p: The long awaited fall in palm oil prices appeared to have started as Malaysian production was building up after February holidays against a background of slow exports, European vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
However they do not expect any significant falls this week.
"We are not going to see a sudden dramatic fall in prices in the coming week, but over the weeks ahead the market will set back," said one.
"Speculators are going to do their best to hold the market, but in the end fundamentals will win," said another trader.
Ivan Wong's latest Malaysian output and stock report seemed to confirm the bearish market outlook although there was little reaction on Friday with players having already discounted the figures.
"Most people will wait for the official data from PORLA next weekend and we don't really expect much to happen this week as a result," said a trader.
In his report the Malaysian private forecaster put output during February at 502,000 tonnes, down 13 percent. In his previous reported Wong estimated a 21 percent drop in production.
Wong projected exports at 440,000 tonnes during February while he put stocks at 670,000 tonnes against 696,272 tonnes in January.

Despite the outlook for lower palm oil prices traders do not see activity picking up. They said this time of year is always quiet while buyers wait for Malaysian palm oil production to recover, and ahead of the south American soybean crop arriving in Europe.

"The market works on a day-to-day basis this time of year because everything is very expensive owing to low output in Malaysia and ahead of fresh soybean supplies coming in from south America," said another.
Traders said another factor keeping the lid on business was the level of fund activity in Chicago.

"When the funds are in control of Chicago it is more like a roulette wheel than a market and bears no relationship to supply and demand, which is another reason why we are only working on a day-to-day basis," said one.
Soft oils are expected to follow the Chicago market but it will not be the main influence on the market.
"What the dollar does against European currencies will be the main factor," said one trader.
Lauric oils are expected to trade in the pattern that has been seen for some weeks with prices supported by slow shipments from origin.
